target.title: [codex] Allow reply_payload_sending to add portable buttons
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins need a channel-portable way to add buttons to outbound replies without turning the broader `message_sending` hook into a transport/presentation mutation API.

This PR lets plugins add portable presentation buttons through the existing `reply_payload_sending` hook. The hook can decorate a normalized `ReplyPayload` with `presentation.blocks` before channel rendering. Telegram then renders those portable button blocks as native inline keyboard buttons, and plugin-owned callback handling can submit the button text back through the normal Telegram callback path.

## Why

Keeping this on `reply_payload_sending` is the cleaner boundary:

- `message_sending` stays focused on logical outbound message behavior such as text, cancellation, and routing.
- `reply_payload_sending` owns presentation-level payload decoration after reply normalization and before channel rendering.
- Channel renderers remain responsible for native button rendering, fallback behavior, and transport-specific limits.

## Behavior Covered

- Plugins can append portable button blocks to reply payloads.
- Telegram renders those portable buttons as inline keyboard buttons.
- Pressing the rendered Telegram button dispatches through the plugin interactive callback path.
- Callback submit text is processed in the interactive dispatch success window.
- If callback submit-text processing fails, the callback dedupe claim is released so the same callback can be retried.
- Policy-skipped callback text is not retried, and the callback dedupe claim is committed.
- `handled: false` plugin callback results still decline ownership and do not submit plugin text or clear buttons.

## Current Head

`6ec4d445a2ce78e40cbd7217d1da0a301a9a1e10`

## Evidence

Maintainer review improvements on the current head:

- Removed unrelated outbound runtime refactoring; retained the bounded Telegram callback result and shared post-handler success window.
- Added policy-skip regression coverage, lifecycle comments, plugin SDK documentation, and release-note context with contributor credit.
- `git diff --check`
- targeted `oxfmt --check` on all nine changed files

Contributor focused validation from the previous patch-identical feature tree:

  - `src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts`: 100 passed

- Result: PASS.
- Validated: bot reply marker observed, plugin-added inline button rendered in Telegram Desktop, TDLib clicked the button, plugin interactive handler fired, and callback reply was observed.
